translationRepairs: Aisin Gioro Manbao, Chen Ce, Shi Shipiao, Lan Tingzhen, his younger cousin Dingyuan, Lin Liang, He Mian, and Chen Lunjiong
Aisin Gioro Manbao, Chen Ce, Shi Shibiao, Lan Tingzhen, his younger cousin Dingyuan, Lin Liang, He Mian, and Chen Lunjiong
施世驃 uses 驃 (biāo); Shipiao is a wrong romanization, and the chapter title already has Shibiao.
Aisin Gioro Manbao, Chen Ce, Shi Shipiao, Lan Tingzhen, younger cousin Dingyuan, Lin Liang, He Mian, Chen Lunjiong
Aisin Gioro Manbao, Chen Ce, Shi Shibiao, Lan Tingzhen, younger cousin Dingyuan, Lin Liang, He Mian, Chen Lunjiong
Literal English has the same wrong Shipiao for 驃; Shibiao is required.
Censor Qu Tingyou argued against the proposal, and the ministry agreed with him.
Censor Qu Tinghu argued against the proposal, and the ministry agreed with him.
廷祜 ends in 祜 (hù); Tingyou misreads the given name as you.
Censor Qu Tingyou argued that this should not be done; the ministry deliberation agreed.
Censor Qu Tinghu argued that this should not be done; the ministry deliberation agreed.
Literal likewise misreads 祜; Qu Tinghu matches 璩廷祜.

In a separate memorial he wrote: "Lukang is the throat of Taiwan, Penghu guards Xiamen, and Anping Town is a key base of the three naval camps. The various sea outlets should be ranked as foremost or secondary points of danger, with redoubts and forts built and patrol garrisons posted;

In a separate memorial he wrote: "Luermen is the throat of Taiwan, Penghu guards Xiamen, and Anping Town is a key base of the three naval camps. The various sea outlets should be ranked as foremost or secondary points of danger, with redoubts and forts built and patrol garrisons posted;
鹿耳門 is Luermen (Deer Ear Gate), a different place from Lukang (鹿港).

In a separate memorial he said: "Lukang is the throat of Taiwan; Penghu is the outer defense of Xiamen; Anping Town is a key post of the three naval camps; and the various sea outlets should be divided into foremost and secondary points of danger, with mounds and forts built and garrison patrols established;

In a separate memorial he said: "Luermen is the throat of Taiwan; Penghu is the outer defense of Xiamen; Anping Town is a key post of the three naval camps; and the various sea outlets should be divided into foremost and secondary points of danger, with mounds and forts built and garrison patrols established;
Literal repeats Lukang for 鹿耳門; Luermen is the correct place name.

Before long Nan'ao regional commander Lan Tingzhen arrived with the fleet. Manbao ordered a combined land-and-sea campaign, joined Naval Commander Shi Shipiao at Penghu, and set a date for the assault.

Before long Nan'ao regional commander Lan Tingzhen arrived with the fleet. Manbao ordered him to command the land and sea forces, join Naval Commander Shi Shibiao at Penghu, and set a date for the assault.
命統水陸軍，會提督施世驃 makes Lan the ordered commander who is to rendezvous with Shi; the original wrongly makes Manbao the subject of 會 and misspells Shibiao.
In the sixth month Shipiao and Tingzhen attacked Lukang, defeated the rebels at Anping, and recovered Taiwan.
In the sixth month Shibiao and Tingzhen attacked Luermen, defeated the rebels at Anping, and recovered Taiwan.
世驃 is Shibiao and 鹿耳門 is Luermen; both original forms are wrong.
In the sixth month Shipiao and Tingzhen attacked Lukang, defeated the rebels at Anping Town, and then recovered Taiwan.
In the sixth month Shibiao and Tingzhen attacked Luermen, defeated the rebels at Anping Town, and then recovered Taiwan.
Literal has the same Shipiao/Lukang errors for 世驃 and 鹿耳門.
Chinese has only 卒, with no 卒官 or other in-office wording; “died in office” invents that detail.
He was summoned to demonstrate horsemanship and archery, ordered to escort grain to Kuisu, and followed Grand General Fiyanggū in pursuit of the enemy to Bayan Ulan.
He was summoned to demonstrate horsemanship and archery, ordered to escort grain to Kuisu, and followed Grand General Maska in pursuit of the enemy to Bayan Ulan.
大將軍馬斯喀 is Maska; Fiyanggū (費揚古) is a different person and is not in this unit.
He was summoned to test his horsemanship and archery, ordered to escort grain transport to Kuisu, and followed the Grand General Fiyanggū in pursuing the enemy to Bayan Ulan.
He was summoned to test his horsemanship and archery, ordered to escort grain transport to Kuisu, and followed the Grand General Maska in pursuing the enemy to Bayan Ulan.
Literal likewise misrenders 馬斯喀 as Fiyanggū; Maska is required.
and that the rebels would surely mass along the central route, so Lukang should be struck directly.
and that the rebels would surely mass along the central route, so Luermen should be struck directly.
宜直搗鹿耳門 names Luermen, not Lukang (鹿港).
he judged the rebels would certainly mass in the central route and that Lukang should be struck directly.
he judged the rebels would certainly mass in the central route and that Luermen should be struck directly.
Literal has the same Lukang mistranslation of 鹿耳門.
In the sixth month they reached Lukang.
In the sixth month they reached Luermen.
抵鹿耳門 means they reached Luermen, not Lukang.
In the sixth month they reached Lukang.
In the sixth month they reached Luermen.
Literal repeats Lukang for 鹿耳門; Luermen is correct.
When the army reached Lukang the rebels held the strategic points and resisted.
When the army reached Luermen the rebels held the strategic points and resisted.
師至鹿耳門 is arrival at Luermen, not Lukang.
When the army reached Lukang the rebels held the strategic points and resisted.
When the army reached Luermen the rebels held the strategic points and resisted.
Literal repeats the same place-name error for 鹿耳門.
His clansman Dingyuan, whose style was Yulin, was a diligent scholar of real ability.
His clansman younger brother Dingyuan, whose style was Yulin, was a diligent scholar of real ability.
族弟 specifically marks a junior clansman (younger brother within the clan); plain “clansman” drops that junior sense.
Naval Commander Shi Shipiao and regional commander Lan Tingzhen, valuing Liang's loyalty and courage, made him vanguard. He led five hundred seventy sailors to Lukang.
Naval Commander Shi Shibiao and regional commander Lan Tingzhen, valuing Liang's loyalty and courage, made him vanguard. He led five hundred seventy sailors to Luermen.
施世驃 is Shibiao and 抵鹿耳門 is Luermen; both original forms are wrong.
Naval Commander Shi Shipiao and Regional Commander Lan Tingzhen, considering Liang loyal and brave, ordered him to serve as vanguard; he led five hundred seventy men of the fleet to Lukang.
Naval Commander Shi Shibiao and Regional Commander Lan Tingzhen, considering Liang loyal and brave, ordered him to serve as vanguard; he led five hundred seventy men of the fleet to Luermen.
Literal has the same Shipiao/Lukang errors for 施世驃 and 鹿耳門.
Knowing Taiwan had just been ravaged by war, Liang paid special attention to pacification and reorganized the land and sea defenses.
Considering that Taiwan had just been ravaged by war, Liang paid special attention to pacification and reorganized the land and sea defenses.
亮以台灣初被兵 uses 以 as “considering that/because”; “Knowing” invents epistemic content and risks a false person reading.
In 1721 he followed Provincial Commander Shi Shipiao against Zhu Yigui. Mian attacked the southern route and captured followers Du Huisan, Su Qing, and others;
In 1721 he followed Provincial Commander Shi Shibiao against Zhu Yigui. Mian attacked the southern route and captured followers Du Huisan, Su Qing, and others;
施世驃 must be romanized Shi Shibiao; Shipiao is wrong.
In the sixtieth year he followed Provincial Commander Shi Shipiao in suppressing Zhu Yigui; Mian attacked the southern route and captured his followers Du Huisan, Su Qing, and others;
In the sixtieth year he followed Provincial Commander Shi Shibiao in suppressing Zhu Yigui; Mian attacked the southern route and captured his followers Du Huisan, Su Qing, and others;

In 1726 rebellious aborigines of communities such as Shuilian Sha stirred. Governor-General Gao Qisuo ordered him to join Taiwan circuit intendant Wu Changzuo in suppressing them.
In 1726 rebellious aborigines of communities such as Shuilian Sha stirred. Governor-General Gao Qizhuo ordered him to join Taiwan circuit intendant Wu Changzuo in suppressing them.
高其倬 ends in 倬 (zhuō); Gao Qisuo misreads the given name.

In the fourth year of Yongzheng the rebellious aborigines of communities such as Shuilian Sha stirred; Governor-General Gao Qisuo ordered him to follow Taiwan Circuit Intendant Wu Changzuo in investigating and punishing them.

In the fourth year of Yongzheng the rebellious aborigines of communities such as Shuilian Sha stirred; Governor-General Gao Qizhuo ordered him to follow Taiwan Circuit Intendant Wu Changzuo in investigating and punishing them.

In 1737 he was transferred to Taiwan, soon moved to Nan'ao, and served as acting naval commander of Fujian.
In 1740 he was transferred to Taiwan, soon moved to Nan'ao, and served as acting naval commander of Fujian.
After 雍正……十年 (s0186) and before 乾隆十年 (s0193), bare 五年 is Qianlong 5 (AD 1740), not 1737.
The rebels seized the prefectural seat. Wancang was killed in battle, and Wenyuan fled to Lukang and drowned himself in the sea.
The rebels seized the prefectural seat. Wancang was killed in battle, and Wenyuan fled to Luermen and drowned himself in the sea.
奔鹿耳門投海死 places the suicide at Luermen, not Lukang.
The rebels took the prefectural seat; Wancang died in battle; Wenyuan fled to Lukang and threw himself into the sea to die.
The rebels took the prefectural seat; Wancang died in battle; Wenyuan fled to Luermen and threw himself into the sea to die.
Literal repeats Lukang for 鹿耳門; Luermen is required.
His son-in-law Cai Zhangqi begged him to stop at his home to settle the family. Chonggong paid no heed, spurred his horse forward, led his men in, and killed many rebels.
His son-in-law Cai Zhangqi grasped his bridle and begged him to stop once at his home to settle the family. Chonggong paid no heed, spurred his horse forward, led his men in, and killed many rebels.
叩馬 is the classic gesture of grasping a rider’s bridle to halt him; the idiomatic English omits that action.

His son-in-law Cai Zhangqi knocked on his horse and begged to pass by his home door once to settle his family; Chonggong paid no heed, leaped on his horse, waved on the crowd, and killed very many rebels.
His son-in-law Cai Zhangqi grasped his bridle and begged to stop by his home once to settle his family; Chonggong paid no heed, leaped on his horse, waved his men on, and killed very many rebels.
叩馬 is grasping the bridle, not knocking on the horse, and 揮眾 means waving the troops onward.
